content.question: How does reinforcement learning differ from supervised learning?
options: RL requires a large labeled dataset, while supervised learning does not.
RL learns by trial-and-error guided by rewards and penalties through interaction with an environment, while supervised learning relies on labeled datasets.
RL predicts continuous values, while supervised learning predicts discrete classes.
RL discovers co-occurrence rules in transaction data, while supervised learning groups similar data points.
content.answer: RL learns by trial-and-error guided by rewards and penalties through interaction with an environment, while supervised learning relies on labeled datasets.
